---
name: builder
description: Implements a target's clone under targets/<t>/clone/ until the dev fixtures pass. Cannot touch the evaluator and cannot see the holdout.
tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
model: opus
---

You implement the clone of one slice of a closed-source product. The target's recorded behaviour
is the specification; your own opinion of how the product "should" work is not.

Read, in order: `targets/<t>/RECON.md`, `targets/<t>/rules.json`, `targets/<t>/adapter.ts` and the
drivers it imports (the exact requests and clicks the clone receives), `targets/<t>/policy.json`,
then the dev fixtures under `targets/<t>/fixtures/dev/`. Some fixtures record screens: an
accessibility tree, the boxes of visible elements (compared within the tolerance the policy
states), a small grey thumbnail (reported, never scored), the calls each step fired, the account
state a flow left behind, or a graph of every screen reachable by clicking. If `targets/<t>/failures.jsonl` exists, read it before proposing.

Loop:

1. Run `npm run verify <t>` first, to see the current state.
2. Pick the rule group with the most failing fixtures in `targets/<t>/verify/failures.json`.
3. Write down, in `targets/<t>/clone/NOTES.md`, the rule as you understand it from the fixtures and
   which fixtures you expect to flip. Then implement it.
4. Run `npm run verify <t>` again. Compare what flipped with your prediction.
5. After two failed attempts on the same rule, delete that part and rewrite it from the fixtures.
   After a third, write in NOTES.md that the rule statement itself looks wrong, and move on.

Constraints:

- Only write under `targets/<t>/clone/`. Fixtures, the lock, the policy, `rules.json`, `harness/`
  and `verify/` are read-only for you, and a hook blocks attempts. Do not look for ways around it.
- The clone never reads fixture files at runtime. Constants you learn from fixtures (static
  fields, defaults) are written in code.
- State lives in memory; `POST /__reset` must restore the seed; the same requests after a reset
  must give the same output (IDs included).
- Do not special-case a fixture by its values. If a behaviour only makes sense as a lookup table,
  say so in NOTES.md.
- `npm run check` must pass when you finish.

Finish with a short report: dev fixtures passing (from the verify output, not from memory), the
rules you could not make pass and why, and anything in the fixtures that contradicts `rules.json`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs one agent headless inside the agent container, on a sandbox copy of the repository that
# holds no holdout, no audit material, no env or scrub files and no git history. The container
# sees only that copy (mounted at /work), not the host file system. The model credential comes
# from .agent.env through --env-file and is never written into the sandbox.
# Usage: harness/sandbox.sh <agent> <target> <task> [copy-back-dir]
# If copy-back-dir is given (for example targets/<t>/clone), that folder alone is copied back.
set -euo pipefail
agent="$1"
target="$2"
task="$3"
copy_back="${4:-}"
repo="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
image="software-clone-factory-agent"
credential="$repo/.agent.env"
stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
log="$repo/targets/$target/logs/$agent-$stamp.jsonl"

command -v docker >/dev/null || { echo "refusing: docker is required (OrbStack or Docker Desktop)" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -f "$credential" ] || { echo "refusing: $credential is missing (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=...)" >&2; exit 2; }
docker image inspect "$image" >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker build -q -t "$image" -f "$repo/harness/docker/Dockerfile" "$repo" >/dev/null

sandbox="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/scf-sandbox-$agent-XXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$sandbox"' EXIT
"$repo/harness/make-sandbox.sh" "$repo" "$sandbox"

mkdir -p "$repo/targets/$target/logs"
# Hours of agent work must not vanish with the sandbox: the clone is copied back even when the run
# fails, and the run's status is returned at the end.
status=0
docker run --rm \
  --env-file "$credential" -e RH_SANDBOX=1 \
  -v "$sandbox:/work" \
  "$image" \
  claude -p "Use the $agent subagent (Agent tool, subagent_type $agent) on target '$target' with this task, following .claude/agents/$agent.md: $task When it finishes, report its final answer verbatim." \
  --model claude-opus-5-5 \
  --permission-mode acceptEdits \
  --allowedTools "Bash Read Write Edit Grep Glob Agent WebFetch" \
  --output-format stream-json --verbose | tee "$log" | jq -rj 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text + "\n"' || status=$?

10	Rules as read from the dev fixtures (checked offline against every logic fixture before coding):
11	
12	- Period: anchored on the start, same day of month (clamped), same time of day (PER-01).
13	- r = period end - proration date, P = period length, e = proration date - period start.
14	- No coupon: credit = -round_half_away(b r / P) on exact integers; flexible charge =
15	  Math.round(n (1 - e / P)) in floating point; classic charge = round_half_up(n r / P). 142 of 142
16	  single-item, no-coupon fixtures agree (PRO-01..04).
17	- A price change without a quantity bills quantity 1 (PRO-10).
18	- Coupons (DSC-04 / MOD-01): classic credit = -round((b - D) r / P) with D the discount the item got
19	  on the invoice that billed the period; flexible credit = -(round(b r/P) - sum round(D_k r/P)).
20	  These two differ by one cent in u-classic-off-once-q4 / u-flex-off-once-q4. Charge =
21	  prorated n minus the prorated discount of the new state (D2 = discounts applied to the new
22	  item alone). All single-coupon dev fixtures agree with these (several formulas are equivalent on
23	  the dev set).
24	- Discount allocation on invoice lines: discounts apply one after another in subscription order;
25	  percent-off per line is floor(base x pct), amount-off per line is floor(total x base / sum);
26	  the rounding remainder goes to the last line.
27	- once coupons: they discount the credited period (the credit carries them) and a once coupon passed
28	  to the preview discounts the remaining-time charge, but never the renewal lines and never appear
29	  in the invoice's `discounts` (DSC-05).

32	  discount at 0; flexible = the first invoice-level discount at 0 (all of them for an immediate
33	  invoice), or, when the invoice has no discount, the discounts the line itself carries.

## Pass 4: corrected rules after holdout batch 1 (DSC-01, DSC-05, DSC-07, DSC-08, INT-02, INV-01)

Baseline (local replay of the 667 logic/lifecycle dev cases): 611 pass, 56 fail: dev-t2-a* (8),
-b* (10), -c* (7), -d* (12), -e* (6), -f* (5), wide2-014/045/053 (credit list), wide2-061/069/290
(credit off by a cent), wide2-281 (allocation). The holdout analysis was read for the rule
statements only; no amount or case ID from it is used in code.

Rules as read from the dev cases:

- DSC-01: percent-off total = round(pct x S) over what is left of the discountable lines,
  spread floor(total x line / S), remainder one cent per line from the last line (same as
  amount-off). The first invoice uses it too, so a flexible credit moves with it. Expected to
  flip: dev-t2-a*, wide2-281, wide2-061/069/290.
- DSC-05: a once coupon passed to the preview is on the invoice (`discounts`,
  `total_discount_amounts`) when the change prorates nothing (it then discounts the renewal) and
  in an immediate invoice (at 0 there). Only a non-immediate invoice with prorations leaves it
  off. Expected: dev-t2-b-noop-* (4), dev-t2-b-always-* (6, with DSC-07).
- DSC-07 (flexible, immediate invoice), credit line list, as the dev cases pin it:
  invoice has no discount -> nothing; credit carried nothing -> the invoice's discounts;
  the carried discounts that survive DSC-08 are none -> nothing; exactly one -> that one (even
  when the invoice's discount is another coupon: dev-t2-c-forever-forever, -c-forever-once,
  -b-always-flexible-forever); two -> the invoice's discounts. The rules.json wording ("lists
  the invoice's discounts unless everything it carries is a used once coupon") disagrees with
  dev-t2-c-forever-forever and dev-t2-b-always-flexible-forever, where a single carried forever
  coupon is listed instead of the passed one. Implemented the fixture reading.
- DSC-08: flexible credit drops a carried discount whose prorated amount round(D r / P) is 0,
  from the description and the line's own list. Expected: dev-t2-d-flexible-* (12),
  dev-t2-e-m2y-flexible-pct-end1.
- INT-02: no "prd < period end" gate any more. A credit with r = 0 and a charge with r2 = 0 are
  omitted; a classic interval change bills a full new period for each changed item even without
  a credit line. Expected: dev-t2-e-*-end0 (6).
- INV-01: an invoice whose amount due is above 0 and below the minimum charge is marked paid,
  amount_due 0, and the amount goes to the customer balance; the next preview shows it as
  starting_balance and adds it to amount_due. Contradiction: rules.json says "below 50
  cents", but dev-t2-f-left50 and dev-t2-f-left51 (50 and 51 cents) are not charged either;
  fresh2-132 (291) is charged. The threshold is somewhere in 52..291. The account is French,
  so the minimum is probably 0.50 EUR converted; the clone uses 59 cents (an assumption, not
  pinned by any dev case). Expected: dev-t2-f-* (5).
